items.detail: Monday's stall became a genuine two-day slide: the **S&P 500 fell 0.32% to 7,728.20**, the **Nasdaq dropped 0.60% to 26,445.45** and the **Dow lost 184.13 points to 53,791.85** — back-to-back losses that leave the index roughly 30 points below its Aug 7 record.
items.why: The US-Iran standoff over reopening the Strait of Hormuz intensified rather than resolved, with Trump demanding Tehran pay reparations in response to Iranian weekend demands, and traders refused to add risk into Wednesday's inflation print.

items.detail: The drag rotated out of chips and into megacap AI: **Alphabet slid 3.6%** — its fourth decline in five sessions — while the **Philadelphia Semiconductor Index actually bucked the tape and rose**, a clean reversal of Monday's Intel-led chip weakness.
items.why: Investors are re-pricing Alphabet's AI bill after it lifted 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205 billion from $180-190 billion and closed a $25 billion senior notes offering with maturities stretching to 2066 to fund data-centre buildout.

items.detail: The energy squeeze has not paused — **Brent is holding above $89 a barrel** after a fifth consecutive session of gains, taking the run to roughly **12% over five days** and pushing crude decisively above Monday's $87.72 settle.
items.why: Signals on a Hormuz deal are contradictory — Pakistan's defence minister says Washington and Tehran are close to an arrangement and Iran-Oman talks are advanced, but Trump's reparations demand cuts the other way, so the risk premium keeps building rather than unwinding.

items.detail: Today's **8:30am ET July CPI** is now explicitly a referendum on the September FOMC: consensus is **3.4% headline year-on-year** (from 3.5%) and **core at 2.5%**, and an upside surprise would hand Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh** the case to raise rates at the **Sept 15-16** meeting.
items.why: Warsh has signalled he is prepared to vote for a hike if inflation runs above expectations and Governor Lisa Cook has publicly backed the same position, so the print lands on a committee already leaning hawkish despite last Friday's weak payrolls.

items.detail: Futures are pointing to a cautiously higher open ahead of the data — **S&P 500 futures +0.11%**, **Nasdaq-100 futures +0.25%** — with **Cisco, Nebius Group and Cerebras Systems** the notable earnings in an otherwise thin calendar before Friday's July retail sales.

Monday's flat finish gave way to a decisive down day: the **Nifty 50 lost 112.10 points (-0.46%) to 24,471.70**, the **Sensex fell 388.19 points (-0.49%) to 78,154.25** and **Bank Nifty slipped 240.70 points (-0.42%) to 57,446.25**, with pharma and IT the only real outperformers against weakness in FMCG, realty and metals.
items.why: A further leg higher in crude, weakness across financials and a softer rupee combined to overwhelm the earnings support that had held the index flat a day earlier.

items.detail: Wednesday's session has broken down badly from a firm start: the Sensex opened **up 109 points at 78,263.33** but was **down 601 points (-0.77%) at 77,552.93** by noon, with the **Nifty off 191 points at 24,280.95** and **Nifty IT falling 2%** as TCS and Infosys led the decline.
items.why: Crude near $90 kept pressure on the import bill while investors cut exposure to dollar-earning IT names ahead of the US CPI release later in the day, turning an opening bounce into the steepest intraday drop of the week.

items.detail: **Godrej Consumer Products crashed 10% to ₹916.20**, a 52-week low and its worst day since December 2024, after the abrupt resignation of MD and CEO **Sudhir Sitapati**, with global CFO **Aasif Malbari** appointed MD & CEO effective immediately.
items.why: The exit was unannounced and unexplained to the market, and coming with the stock already about 30% below its ₹1,308.40 52-week high it raised immediate questions about strategy continuity rather than being read as a routine succession.

items.detail: The FII picture is better than the tape suggests and has flipped from the selling narrative: foreign investors have **bought a net $1.5 billion of Indian equities in August so far**, following **$2.1 billion of inflows in July** — though they remain net sellers of a record **$25.7 billion in 2026**.
items.why: Softening US rate expectations after the July payrolls miss have pulled foreign money back into Indian equities over the past six weeks, meaning the current weakness is being driven by crude and stock-specific shocks rather than by foreign outflows.

items.detail: India's **July retail inflation lands today**, with a Reuters poll centring on **4.50%** and a Mint poll on an unchanged **4.4%** versus June's **4.38%** — either outcome would be a second straight month above the RBI's 4% medium-term target.
items.why: Forecasters expect food inflation to broaden across key items while the delayed pass-through of the Middle East energy shock continues to lift transport costs, leaving the risks tilted to the upside.

items.detail: The break below $65,000 has extended rather than stabilised: **Bitcoin fell about 1.69% to roughly $63,907** on Tuesday and has slipped further to around **$63,495** overnight, while **Ether has now lost $1,900** outright after failing to clear it for days.
items.why: Traders cut risk ahead of the US CPI release, and Brent pushing above $89 on the collapse in Hormuz deal optimism revived exactly the inflation fear that has been capping crypto since the weekend.

items.detail: The move was amplified by forced selling rather than fresh distribution — roughly **$49.6 million of bitcoin liquidations**, of which more than **$47 million were long positions**, were wiped out on the rejection at $65,000.
items.why: Leverage had built up on the assumption that $65,000 would hold as support after four sessions of defending it, so the break flushed crowded longs and accelerated the decline beyond what spot selling alone would have produced.

items.detail: Solana's ETF drought has broken: spot SOL funds took in **$8.8 million on Aug 10**, the strongest day since **May 12**, with Bitwise's **BSOL absorbing nearly the entire $8.83 million** and lifting total SOL ETF net assets to about **$906 million** — even as **SOL slipped 1.16% to $74.88**.
items.why: Institutional allocators stepped back in after July and early-August flows went dormant, reversing the outflow pattern that had left SOL with no marginal buyer, though the sums are still far too small to move spot against a risk-off tape.

items.detail: The bitcoin ETF inflow streak is now fully tallied at **$853.5 million across Aug 3-7** — a roughly **$915 million swing** from the prior week's $61.5 million of outflows — with **BlackRock's IBIT taking $693 million, or 81% of the total**, pushing cumulative net inflows since launch to **$52.18 billion**.
items.why: The concentration in a single fund shows the bid is coming from large allocators rebalancing into bitcoin on the view that a weakening labour market caps the Fed, not from broad retail participation, which is why it has not translated into spot price support.

items.detail: Today's **8:30am ET CPI is the binary event for the tape**: a cool print gives Bitcoin a route back toward the **$65,000** level it lost this week, while a hot one revives September hike risk with BTC already sitting on the lower edge of its descending channel near **$62,900**.

crossCuttingTheme: Brent's fifth straight advance to above $89 — a roughly 12% five-day run on the failure of US-Iran Hormuz talks — has now compounded into a second down session everywhere at once: it drove the S&P 500's back-to-back losses alongside Alphabet's AI-capex slide, knocked the Sensex 601 points intraday by worsening India's import-cost and inflation math days before its own CPI, and pushed Bitcoin under $64,000 as leveraged longs were liquidated, leaving today's 8:30am ET July CPI as the single release that decides whether Fed Chair Warsh gets the cover to hike in September or the energy spike is written off as transitory.
